name: Roundabout from above
meaning: Aerial view of a single-lane roundabout: a grassy center island ringed by a reddish truck apron, with four roads entering it, raised splitter islands and crosswalks on each approach.
author: Oregon Department of Transportation

name: School bus stop arm, driver's view
meaning: View from the driver's seat of a car: a yellow school bus right in front has its red STOP arm extended from its side.
author: Katy Warner

name: Flashing yellow left-turn arrow
meaning: Two traffic signals over a road: the left-turn signal shows a yellow left arrow in its third light position, while the signal for straight-ahead traffic shows a green light.
author: Deloreanman14

name: Rural crossing with crossbucks only
meaning: A gravel road crosses a railroad track in open country. The crossing is marked only by white X-shaped RAILROAD CROSSING signs on posts, with no lights or gates.
author: YosemiteYamper

name: Railroad crossing gates down
meaning: A city railroad crossing with its red-and-white striped gate arms lowered across the road and a red warning light lit on the signal mast.
author: Eric Fischer

name: Carpool (HOV) lane sign
meaning: An overhead sign above the left lane of a freeway shows a white diamond and reads CARPOOLS ONLY, 2 OR MORE PERSONS PER VEHICLE, with an arrow pointing down to the lane.
author: Coolcaesar

name: Two-way center left-turn lane
meaning: A multi-lane road with a center lane bordered on each side by a solid yellow line and a broken yellow line, with a white turn arrow painted in the lane.
author: DanTD

name: Green-painted bike lane
meaning: A green-painted bike lane on a multi-lane road where drivers turning off onto a ramp must cross the bike lane; the green paint marks the crossing area.
author: Atomic Taco

name: Shared-lane marking (sharrow)
meaning: A city street in New York with a shared-lane marking, a bicycle symbol with two chevrons above it, painted in the travel lane next to a crosswalk.
author: Jim.henderson

name: Shoulder rumble strip
meaning: Close-up of a paved highway shoulder next to the white edge line, with a band of grooves (a rumble strip) cut across the pavement.
author: Visviva

name: Entrance ramp merging onto a freeway
meaning: Two cars on an entrance ramp heading to merge onto a busy divided interstate highway, seen from behind.
author: KOMUnews

name: Divided highway with median
meaning: An interstate highway seen from an overpass: two lanes in each direction separated by a wide grassy median, with a solid yellow edge line on the median side of each roadway and a white edge line on the outside.
author: Jakec

name: Flooded road
meaning: A two-lane road with a double yellow center line disappears under brown floodwater ahead; a white truck is stopped at the left edge of the road in the foreground.
author: U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service

name: Deer crossing the road
meaning: A white-tailed deer walks across a curving two-lane road with a double yellow center line, next to woods.
author: Dwight Burdette

name: Work zone on a two-lane road
meaning: Driver's view of a two-lane road in a work zone: orange cones line the lane, orange diamond warning signs stand on the shoulder, and construction equipment is working ahead.
author: Oregon Department of Transportation

name: Highway work zone lane closure
meaning: Trucks and cars move in single file past a highway work zone where a long row of orange-and-white drums closes off a lane.
author: Oregon Department of Transportation

name: Car driving in thick fog
meaning: A car drives on a road in thick fog that hides the trees and the road ahead.
author: U.S. Forest Service, San Bernardino National Forest

name: Traffic in falling snow
meaning: Heavy traffic with headlights on moves along a snow-covered city street while snow falls.
author: Oregon Department of Transportation

name: Ambulance responding
meaning: A red-and-white ambulance with its emergency lights on drives along a city street toward the camera.
author: Noah Wulf

name: Horse-drawn buggy on a highway
meaning: A horse-drawn buggy travels along the edge of a curving two-lane rural highway.
author: Jakec

name: Farm tractor on a highway
meaning: A large green farm tractor travels on a two-lane highway, with a line of cars and a truck following close behind it.
author: Oregon Department of Transportation

name: School crossing guards
meaning: School crossing guards in bright safety vests hold up STOP paddles while children walk and ride bikes across a marked crosswalk next to a yellow-green school crossing sign.
author: Austin Transportation and Public Works

name: Pedestrians in a crosswalk
meaning: Several people, seen from behind, walk across a wide street in a marked crosswalk with white bars at a city intersection.
author: Downtowngal

name: Pedestrian hybrid beacon
meaning: A pedestrian hybrid beacon, two red lights above one yellow light, hangs dark on a mast arm over a marked crosswalk on a suburban road.
author: William F. Yurasko

name: Motorcycle group in staggered formation
meaning: A group of motorcyclists rides on a U.S. highway in a staggered formation, alternating between the left and right sides of the lane.
author: Cpl. Peter R. Miller, U.S. Marine Corps
